PRODUCED FROM CUSTODIAN MAILBOX: d.kessler@talvernlogistics.example — Bates TLG-EM-0414 through TLG-EM-0416
CONFIDENTIAL — SUBJECT TO PROTECTIVE ORDER, Meridian Grain Cooperative, Inc. v. Talvern Logistics Group LLC, No. 0:25-cv-01877

---- Message 3 of 3 ----
From: Dana Kessler, VP Operations, Talvern Logistics Group LLC
To: Ruth Okafor, Site Manager, Silo Complex 4 (Halden Junction)
Cc: Priya Natarajan, Regional Energy Desk
Date: Friday, March 14, 2025, 4:47 PM CT
Subject: RE: RE: Q1 energy overrun — Complex 4 action

Ruth — decision is made. Effective tonight, take dehumidification units DH-4A, DH-4B, DH-4C and DH-4D at Complex 4 offline on the load-shed schedule, 22:00 to 06:00, and if the demand-charge numbers hold, keep them dark through the shoulder season. Priya's model says Complex 4 climate control is 61 percent of the site's demand charge and we are not clawing back the Q1 overrun any other way.

I am aware of what the Meridian contract says. Section 6.2 of the Warehousing and Climate Services Agreement calls for continuous dehumidification and a ceiling of 55 percent relative humidity in the storage galleries. If Meridian asks, this is routine maintenance on the air-handling side. Log it that way in the site diary. I will take the heat if Meridian notices.

Do not route this through the maintenance ticketing queue — handle it as a local operating instruction from this office.

— DK

---- Message 2 of 3 ----
From: Ruth Okafor
To: Dana Kessler
Date: Friday, March 14, 2025, 3:58 PM CT
Subject: RE: Q1 energy overrun — Complex 4 action

Dana — before I touch those units I want it in writing. The galleries are holding 1.04 million bushels of Meridian hard red spring wheat right now and the loggers have us at 52 to 54 percent RH with all four units running. If we shed them overnight in March we will drift over spec within days. Please confirm you are directing the power-down notwithstanding the WCSA humidity clause.

---- Message 1 of 3 ----
From: Priya Natarajan, Regional Energy Desk
To: Dana Kessler
Date: Thursday, March 13, 2025, 11:12 AM CT
Subject: Q1 energy overrun — Complex 4 action

Dana — attached is the demand-charge workup. Complex 4 is the outlier in the region. The only lever big enough this quarter is the dehumidification bank. Flagging for your call; this desk does not have authority over leased-site climate equipment.

documents.body:
PRODUCED FROM CUSTODIAN MAILBOX: r.okafor@talvernlogistics.example — Bates TLG-EM-0419
CONFIDENTIAL — SUBJECT TO PROTECTIVE ORDER, Meridian Grain Cooperative, Inc. v. Talvern Logistics Group LLC, No. 0:25-cv-01877

From: Ruth Okafor, Site Manager, Silo Complex 4 (Halden Junction)
To: Dana Kessler, VP Operations
Cc: Night Shift Distribution — Complex 4
Date: Saturday, March 15, 2025, 7:21 AM CT
Subject: Complex 4 — load-shed executed per your 3/14 instruction

Dana —

Confirming execution of your written instruction of yesterday afternoon. Units DH-4A through DH-4D were de-energized at 23:10 last night by the night crew. Per your direction the action is entered in the site diary as 'routine maintenance — air handling, scheduled,' and no ticket was opened in the maintenance queue.

Two operational notes for the record:

1. Alarm handling. The gallery humidity sensors are hard-wired to the annunciator panel and would have chimed continuously overnight. I authorized the shift lead to mute the RH set-point alarms for the duration of the load-shed window so the panel is not screaming at the crew. The mute is logged on the panel itself.

2. Drift. As of the 06:30 walk-through this morning the north gallery loggers read 58 percent RH and the south gallery 63 percent RH, against the 55 percent ceiling in the Meridian agreement. That is one night. If the units stay dark on the schedule you described — and certainly if they stay dark through the shoulder season — the galleries will run well over spec and the wheat will take on moisture. I have said my piece on this and will follow the instruction as given.

Re-energization will occur only on written direction from your office, per your note. The crew has standing instructions not to restart the bank on their own initiative.

Ruth Okafor
Site Manager, Complex 4 — Halden Junction
Talvern Logistics Group LLC

documents.title: Discovery-retrieval pack — Calder & Voss engineering report: Silo Complex 4 data-logger analysis (2025-06-18)
documents.body:
CALDER & VOSS CONSULTING ENGINEERS, PLLC
Forensic Mechanical Systems Practice — Report No. CV-2025-0611
June 18, 2025

Prepared for: Harwick & Sloane LLP, counsel for Meridian Grain Cooperative, Inc.
Re: Meridian Grain Cooperative, Inc. v. Talvern Logistics Group LLC, No. 0:25-cv-01877 — continuity of dehumidification outage, Silo Complex 4, Halden Junction

1. Assignment. Counsel asked this firm to determine, from physical and electronic records, whether the dehumidification bank serving Silo Complex 4 (units DH-4A through DH-4D) was out of service continuously during the spring 2025 period, or only intermittently (for example, on an overnight-only schedule). Counsel emphasized that the produced custodian correspondence describes an overnight load-shed schedule and contains post-hoc speculation, but does not itself establish continuity of the outage.

2. Materials examined. (a) Twelve onboard interval data loggers recovered from the gallery sensor network under the parties' inspection protocol of May 29, 2025; (b) non-volatile memory images from the DH-4 motor-control-center controllers; (c) utility interval billing data for meter 771-HJ-04; (d) the Complex 4 site diary.

3. Findings.
3.1 Controller NVRAM for all four units records a de-energization event at 23:10 CT on March 14, 2025, and no subsequent re-energization event until 06:40 CT on April 20, 2025. There are no intervening start commands, manual or scheduled, in any of the four controller logs.
3.2 The gallery logger series corroborate the controller record: interior relative humidity rises monotonically from March 15, crossing the 55 percent contractual ceiling on March 17, and remains above that ceiling for 892 consecutive logged hours, with a period mean of 71 percent RH and a peak of 84 percent RH on April 11.
3.3 Utility interval data show the site's demand profile dropping by an amount consistent with the full dehumidification bank being offline continuously, not on a 22:00-06:00 cycle. An overnight-only shed would present as a diurnal sawtooth; none is present after March 14.
3.4 The site diary entries describing 'routine maintenance — air handling' are inconsistent with the controller record, which shows no maintenance lockouts, test starts, or service cycling during the period.

4. Opinion. To a reasonable degree of engineering certainty, units DH-4A through DH-4D were continuously de-energized from 23:10 CT on March 14, 2025 through 06:40 CT on April 20, 2025, and gallery humidity exceeded the 55 percent ceiling continuously from March 17 through April 20. The continuity of the outage is established by the instrument record analyzed here; it cannot be established from the correspondence alone.

Marta Calder, P.E. — Principal
Calder & Voss Consulting Engineers, PLLC

From: Marta Calder, P.E. <m.calder@caldervoss.example>
To: Adaeze Reyes, Harwick & Sloane LLP <a.reyes@harwicksloane.example>
Cc: Tom Voss, P.E.; Records, Calder & Voss
Date: Thursday, June 19, 2025, 9:04 AM CT
Subject: Transmittal — Report CV-2025-0611 and logger extract CV-DL-88 (Meridian v. Talvern)

Counsel —

Transmitted with this message are (1) the executed original of our Report No. CV-2025-0611, dated June 18, 2025, and (2) extract CV-DL-88, the machine-readable interval series underlying Sections 3.1 through 3.3 of the report.

For your working summary: the extract covers all twelve gallery loggers and all four motor-control-center controllers at Silo Complex 4. The interval data shows no re-energization events between the de-energization at 23:10 CT on March 14, 2025 and the restart at 06:40 CT on April 20, 2025. Every logged hour in between shows the bank drawing zero load. The 892-consecutive-hour excursion above the 55 percent relative-humidity ceiling appears in the extract as an unbroken run; we did not interpolate or smooth any interval.

Chain of custody: the loggers and controller images were collected under the May 29, 2025 inspection protocol in the presence of representatives of both parties; imaging hashes were exchanged on site and are reproduced at tab C of the report. Extract CV-DL-88 was generated from the working copies on June 17, 2025, and the generation script and its output hash are included in the extract package so your vendor can reproduce the series independently.

Please note our standard caveat: this firm's analysis addresses the physical and electronic record only. We express no view on contractual interpretation or on any party's state of mind, and nothing in the extract should be cited as evidence of who directed the outage — that is outside the instrument record.

Invoice under separate cover per the retention letter.

Regards,
Marta Calder, P.E.
Calder & Voss Consulting Engineers, PLLC — Forensic Mechanical Systems Practice

TALVERN LOGISTICS GROUP LLC
MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS
April 2, 2025 — 10:00 AM CT — Talvern headquarters, boardroom A, and by video conference
Bates TLG-BRD-2025-04 — PRODUCED SUBJECT TO PROTECTIVE ORDER, No. 0:25-cv-01877

Present: Chair E. Talvern-Whitcomb; Directors S. Marchetti (also General Counsel and Secretary), H. Bloor, K. Osei, R. Fontaine, L. Adler, J. Whitcomb-Pryce. Also attending for portions: Chief Financial Officer N. Grieve.

1. Call to order; quorum. The Chair called the meeting to order at 10:02 AM and the Secretary confirmed a quorum of seven directors.

2. Approval of prior minutes. The minutes of the February 5, 2025 regular meeting were approved as circulated.

3. First-quarter financial review. CFO Grieve presented the first-quarter management accounts, noting the energy cost overrun previously reported to the Board and management's containment work in response. Discussion followed regarding demand charges at leased storage sites and fleet fuel spend.

4. Cost Containment Initiative CC-7. CFO Grieve presented for adoption the cost containment program designated CC-7, as set out in management memorandum TLG-FIN-22 dated March 28, 2025, previously circulated to all directors. The Chair noted that the memorandum is incorporated into these minutes by reference and its contents are not restated here. Upon motion duly made by Director Bloor and seconded by Director Osei, the Board unanimously adopted the following resolution by a vote of 7-0:

RESOLUTION 2025-09. RESOLVED, that the Cost Containment Initiative designated CC-7, as presented to the Board in management memorandum TLG-FIN-22 dated March 28, 2025, is hereby ADOPTED AND RATIFIED in all respects, including the implementation steps already taken by management under that initiative; and FURTHER RESOLVED, that management is authorized and directed to continue implementation of CC-7 through fiscal year end and to report quarterly to the Board on realized savings.

5. Other business. None.

6. Adjournment. There being no further business, the meeting adjourned at 11:14 AM.

Respectfully submitted,
S. Marchetti, Secretary

documents.title: Discovery-retrieval pack — Talvern memorandum TLG-FIN-22: scope of Cost Containment Initiative CC-7 (2025-03-28)
documents.body:
TALVERN LOGISTICS GROUP LLC — MANAGEMENT MEMORANDUM
No. TLG-FIN-22 — March 28, 2025
From: N. Grieve, Chief Financial Officer
To: The Board of Directors
Re: Definition and scope of Cost Containment Initiative CC-7
Bates TLG-FIN-0022 — PRODUCED SUBJECT TO PROTECTIVE ORDER, No. 0:25-cv-01877

Directors —

This memorandum defines the cost containment program that management has designated Initiative CC-7 and that will be presented for Board adoption at the April 2, 2025 meeting. Management began implementing certain CC-7 measures in mid-March under existing operating authority; Board adoption will ratify those steps and authorize continuation.

Scope of Initiative CC-7. The initiative comprises four measures:

(i) Fleet idle-reduction. Governor reprogramming and idle-shutdown timers across the linehaul fleet. Projected annualized savings: 1.9 million dollars.

(ii) Lease consolidation. Non-renewal of two third-party cross-dock leases (Cedar Falls and Roseau) at term. Projected annualized savings: 1.1 million dollars.

(iii) Suspension of active climate-control operations at leased grain-storage sites, including Silo Complex 4 at Halden Junction operated under the Meridian Warehousing and Climate Services Agreement. The dehumidification bank at Complex 4 is the largest single contributor to regional demand charges. Operations has placed the Complex 4 units on an extended shed beginning March 14, 2025. Projected savings through the shoulder season: 640,000 dollars. Management notes for completeness that the Meridian agreement contains climate specifications; operations assesses the commercial exposure as manageable relative to the projected savings.

(iv) Deferral of non-safety maintenance. Deferral of cosmetic and non-safety facility maintenance across the network to fiscal 2026. Projected savings: 700,000 dollars.

Governance. Measures (i), (ii) and (iv) are within routine management authority. Measure (iii) touches a customer contract and is therefore included in the resolution presented for adoption, so that the Board's action covers the program as a whole, including steps already taken.

N. Grieve
Chief Financial Officer

HARWICK & SLOANE LLP
Attorneys at Law — Minneapolis
July 14, 2025

BY EMAIL
Jonas Pell, Esq.
Dunmore Pell LLP
Counsel for Talvern Logistics Group LLC

Re: Meridian Grain Cooperative, Inc. v. Talvern Logistics Group LLC, No. 0:25-cv-01877 — meet and confer of July 11, 2025; Talvern custodian ESI production costs

Dear Mr. Pell:

This letter memorializes the parties' July 11 meet and confer under the Court's ESI protocol and Rule 26(f), concerning the cost of collecting, processing, reviewing and producing the Talvern custodian ESI hosted by our vendor, Veritas Row Discovery Services.

First, the parties agreed that the operative statement of the total production cost for the Talvern custodian ESI is the figure set out in Veritas Row's Revised Statement of Work No. 2 dated July 9, 2025: 412,500 dollars, covering nine custodians and three production waves. As we discussed, the vendor's earlier estimate of late June was prepared before custodian interviews, assumed a smaller custodian count and collection volume, and has been superseded; neither party will rely on it for any purpose, including cost-shifting argument.

Second, on allocation: without prejudice to either party's position on ultimate taxation of costs, the parties agreed to proceed on a 60/40 split of the total stated above (Meridian 60 percent, Talvern 40 percent), subject to reallocation by the Court on motion after substantial completion of the production waves.

Third, scheduling: wave one substantial completion by August 15, 2025; waves two and three at thirty-day intervals thereafter; privilege logs to follow each wave within twenty-one days.

If this letter does not accurately record your understanding of the July 11 conference, please advise in writing within seven days; otherwise we will treat the above as the parties' agreement and will so represent to the Court in the joint status report.

Very truly yours,
Adaeze Reyes
Partner, Harwick & Sloane LLP

documents.title: Discovery-retrieval pack — Inventory valuation memo: spoiled grain lots, Silo Complex 4 (2025-05-20)
documents.body:
MERIDIAN GRAIN COOPERATIVE, INC. — INTERNAL MEMORANDUM (PRIVILEGED PORTIONS REDACTED FOR PRODUCTION)
May 20, 2025
From: Oskar Brandt, Chief Financial Officer, with G. Lindqvist, Senior Grain Merchandiser
To: Adaeze Reyes, Harwick & Sloane LLP
Re: Final valuation of spoiled inventory, Silo Complex 4, Halden Junction

1. Purpose and limitation. This memorandum states the cooperative's final valuation of the grain destroyed by the humidity excursion at Silo Complex 4. This memorandum values only the destroyed inventory. It does not include replacement or cover costs, which are addressed in the separate cover purchase summary being prepared by the merchandising desk, and it does not include incidental handling, disposal or fumigation charges.

2. Affected inventory. Storage lots 41 through 58, comprising 1,040,000 bushels of No. 1 hard red spring wheat, 13.5 percent protein basis, placed into the Complex 4 galleries between September 2024 and February 2025. State grain inspection on May 6-8, 2025 graded the affected lots as sample grade due to moisture damage, heat damage and mold, with the inspection certificates attached at tab B.

3. Methodology. Each lot is valued at the Chicago Board of Trade reference price for the applicable delivery month as of the grading date, adjusted for the cooperative's historical Halden Junction basis, protein premium, and freight to the primary delivery market, less the realized salvage value obtained at auction for the sample-grade material (feed and industrial use). Lot-by-lot detail appears at tab C. No lost-profit, interest or consequential element is included in this figure.

4. Result. The final spoiled-inventory loss, net of salvage, is 6,240,000 dollars. This figure replaces all earlier working numbers circulated internally while grading and salvage were pending, and it is the number the cooperative will stand behind in this litigation for the destroyed-inventory component.

5. Reliance. The merchandising desk's price and basis worksheets, the inspection certificates, and the salvage auction settlement sheets are maintained in the matter file and are available for expert review.

Oskar Brandt, CFO
Meridian Grain Cooperative, Inc.

documents.title: Discovery-retrieval pack — Cover purchase summary: replacement grain procurement premium (2025-05-27)
documents.body:
MERIDIAN GRAIN COOPERATIVE, INC. — MERCHANDISING DESK SUMMARY (PRODUCED IN DISCOVERY)
May 27, 2025
From: G. Lindqvist, Senior Grain Merchandiser
To: Oskar Brandt, CFO; Adaeze Reyes, Harwick & Sloane LLP
Re: Cover purchases to meet delivery obligations — final premium computation

1. Background. At the time the Complex 4 spoilage was discovered, the cooperative carried forward-delivery obligations to two flour millers — Askel Milling Company (Duluth) and Prairie Hearth Mills (Fargo) — deliverable May through August 2025, which had been allocated against the Complex 4 stocks. To avoid default on those contracts the desk executed cover purchases of equivalent No. 1 hard red spring wheat, 13.5 percent protein basis, in the cash market between May 9 and May 23, 2025.

2. What this summary measures. This summary states the incremental cost of cover only: the premium of the cover purchase prices over the contract benchmark prices embedded in the miller contracts, plus the freight differential arising from sourcing out-of-position bushels (primarily ex-elevator Minot and Aberdeen rather than Halden Junction). It deliberately excludes the value of the spoiled inventory itself, which is stated in the CFO's inventory valuation memorandum of May 20, 2025, so that the two components can be added without double counting.

3. Computation. Eleven cover trades totaling 1,010,000 bushels. Weighted average cover price premium over contract benchmark: 2.06 dollars per bushel, for 2,080,600 dollars. Freight differential on out-of-position origination, net of saved Halden Junction elevation: 329,400 dollars. Both figures are drawn from executed trade confirmations and rate confirmations at tabs A and B.

4. Result. The final cover-purchase premium is 2,410,000 dollars. The desk considers this figure final; all trades are settled and no further cover is anticipated for the affected delivery windows.

5. Notes. Both miller counterparties accepted the substituted deliveries without claim. Demurrage was avoided. The desk makes no legal characterization of recoverability; that is for counsel.

G. Lindqvist
Senior Grain Merchandiser, Meridian Grain Cooperative, Inc.

documents.title: Discovery-retrieval pack — Meridian special board meeting minutes: settlement authority vote (2025-08-01)
documents.body:
MERIDIAN GRAIN COOPERATIVE, INC.
MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS
August 1, 2025 — 2:00 PM CT — cooperative offices, Halden Junction, and by telephone

Present: President and Chair A. Sundstrom; Directors M. Halvorsen, T. Ruiz, C. Bergstrom, D. Okonkwo, F. Lindahl, P. Vasquez. Also present by invitation: O. Brandt, CFO; A. Reyes of Harwick & Sloane LLP, litigation counsel.

1. Call to order; notice; quorum. The Chair called the special meeting to order at 2:03 PM. The Secretary confirmed that notice of the special meeting was duly given and that a quorum of seven directors was present.

2. Purpose. The Chair stated that the special meeting was called to consider (a) the settlement offer received from Talvern Logistics Group LLC in the pending litigation, and (b) ratification of the amended engagement terms with litigation counsel.

3. Settlement offer. Ms. Reyes reported that by letter dated July 22, 2025, counsel for Talvern conveyed an offer of 2,100,000 dollars in full settlement of all claims, conditioned on a complete release and containing no admission of liability, open for twenty-one days. Ms. Reyes reviewed the offer against the damages components previously reported to the Board and answered directors' questions concerning litigation risk, expected costs through trial, and the spoliation issues under investigation. Director Halvorsen moved that the cooperative accept the offer as presented; Director Ruiz seconded the motion for purposes of discussion. After discussion, the Chair called the question. THE MOTION FAILED, two votes in favor (Halvorsen, Ruiz) and five opposed (Sundstrom, Bergstrom, Okonkwo, Lindahl, Vasquez). No settlement authority was granted, and the Board directed counsel to communicate the rejection of the offer and to proceed with the litigation, including the contemplated spoliation motion practice.

4. Ratification of amended engagement terms. On motion duly made and seconded, the Board voted 7-0 to ratify the First Amendment to the engagement letter with Harwick & Sloane LLP dated June 2, 2025, including the revised litigation fee budget of 1,975,000 dollars through trial stated therein.

5. Adjournment. The meeting adjourned at 3:26 PM.

Respectfully submitted,
C. Bergstrom, Secretary

documents.body:
DUNMORE PELL LLP
Counselors at Law — Saint Paul
July 22, 2025

BY EMAIL — SUBJECT TO FED. R. EVID. 408 AND ALL STATE ANALOGUES
Adaeze Reyes, Esq.
Harwick & Sloane LLP
Counsel for Meridian Grain Cooperative, Inc.

Re: Meridian Grain Cooperative, Inc. v. Talvern Logistics Group LLC, No. 0:25-cv-01877 — offer of compromise

Dear Ms. Reyes:

This letter is a confidential offer of compromise made solely to avoid the burden and expense of continued litigation. Nothing in it is or may be construed as an admission of liability, fault, or the truth of any allegation in the complaint, all of which Talvern Logistics Group LLC continues to deny.

On behalf of Talvern, we are authorized to offer 2,100,000 dollars, payable within thirty days of execution of a settlement agreement, in full and final settlement of all claims that were or could have been asserted in the above-captioned action, conditioned on: (a) a complete mutual release of all claims arising from or relating to the Warehousing and Climate Services Agreement and the storage of the cooperative's grain at Silo Complex 4; (b) dismissal of the action with prejudice, each party to bear its own fees and costs; (c) withdrawal of the cooperative's pending preservation and spoliation correspondence and any contemplated motion practice thereon; and (d) customary confidentiality and non-disparagement terms.

In our client's view this offer should be measured against the genuine disputes in the case, including causation of the claimed grading outcomes, the cooperative's own monitoring obligations under Section 4.7 of the agreement, and the substantial cost both parties face through expert discovery and trial.

This offer remains open for twenty-one days from the date of this letter, after which it is withdrawn without further notice. It may be accepted only in a writing signed by our client.

Very truly yours,
Jonas Pell
Dunmore Pell LLP
Counsel for Talvern Logistics Group LLC

S. Marchetti

FIRST AMENDMENT TO ENGAGEMENT LETTER
June 2, 2025

This First Amendment amends the engagement letter dated August 30, 2024 (the 'Engagement Letter') between HARWICK & SLOANE LLP (the 'Firm') and MERIDIAN GRAIN COOPERATIVE, INC. (the 'Client') with respect to the matter styled Meridian Grain Cooperative, Inc. v. Talvern Logistics Group LLC, No. 0:25-cv-01877 (the 'Litigation').

Recitals. The Engagement Letter was executed when the dispute was in its pre-suit posture and set a litigation fee budget of 1,600,000 dollars through trial. Since execution, the scope of the Litigation has expanded materially: the parties' agreed ESI protocol added Talvern custodians and a vendor-hosted review; the Client has retained a forensic engineering expert; and counsel anticipates spoliation motion practice concerning the timing of Talvern's preservation efforts. The parties therefore agree to revise the budget and related terms as stated below. The original 1,600,000 dollar budget figure in Section 2 of the Engagement Letter is superseded in its entirety by this Amendment and is of no further effect.

1. Revised fee budget. Section 2 of the Engagement Letter is amended to state: 'The Firm's litigation fee budget for the Litigation, covering all phases through entry of judgment after trial but excluding any appeal, is 1,975,000 dollars. The Firm will notify the Client in writing when sixty percent and eighty-five percent of the budget have been incurred, and will not exceed the budget without the Client's prior written consent.'

2. Staffing. The core team remains A. Reyes (lead partner), two associates and one discovery counsel; the parties approve the addition of one senior associate for expert and motion practice at the rates in Schedule A, as revised.

documents.body:
PRODUCED FROM CUSTODIAN MAILBOX: d.kessler@talvernlogistics.example — Bates TLG-EM-0388
CONFIDENTIAL — SUBJECT TO PROTECTIVE ORDER, Meridian Grain Cooperative, Inc. v. Talvern Logistics Group LLC, No. 0:25-cv-01877

From: Dana Kessler, VP Operations, Talvern Logistics Group LLC
To: Wade Corliss, Regional Maintenance Lead
Cc: Site Manager Distribution — Complex 2 (Brainerd)
Date: Friday, February 21, 2025, 8:40 AM CT
Subject: Complex 2 — DH-2B compressor fault, service power-down window

Wade —

The annunciator at Complex 2 flagged a recurring compressor over-current fault on dehumidification unit DH-2B this week. Please schedule a service power-down for that unit only, Monday February 24, window 08:00 to 14:00, with restoration the same day. Open a ticket in the maintenance queue in the ordinary course and attach the fault log — I want this one fully papered since the unit is still under the manufacturer's extended warranty and we may claim the compressor.

Housekeeping notes for the file:

1. Scope. This is a single-unit service outage at Complex 2 in Brainerd. Units DH-2A and DH-2C carry the gallery load during the window; the site engineer projects relative humidity will hold within operating range throughout. No load-shedding, energy program or schedule change is involved — this is a repair.

2. Customer impact. Meridian product is not stored at Complex 2; the Brainerd galleries hold Talvern's own transload buffer stock and two spot-market customers, both of whose storage terms permit scheduled maintenance windows on notice. Front office will send the standard notice today.

3. Parts. If the compressor swap runs past 14:00, do not extend the outage — re-energize on the redundant units' rotation and reschedule the balance of the work for the following Monday under a fresh ticket.

Confirm the window by end of day.

— DK
Dana Kessler, VP Operations
Talvern Logistics Group LLC

documents.title: Discovery-retrieval pack — Talvern Logistics board minutes: energy cost review deferred (2025-02-05)
documents.body:
TALVERN LOGISTICS GROUP LLC
MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS
February 5, 2025 — 10:00 AM CT — Talvern headquarters, boardroom A, and by video conference
Bates TLG-BRD-2025-02 — PRODUCED SUBJECT TO PROTECTIVE ORDER, No. 0:25-cv-01877

Present: Chair E. Talvern-Whitcomb; Directors S. Marchetti (also General Counsel and Secretary), H. Bloor, K. Osei, R. Fontaine, L. Adler, J. Whitcomb-Pryce. Also attending for portions: Chief Financial Officer N. Grieve.

1. Call to order; quorum. The Chair called the meeting to order at 10:04 AM and the Secretary confirmed a quorum.

2. Approval of prior minutes. The minutes of the December 3, 2024 regular meeting were approved as circulated.

3. Preliminary energy cost review. CFO Grieve presented a preliminary review of network energy costs, noting that fourth-quarter demand charges ran above plan and that climate-control spend at leased storage sites — including the dehumidification banks at the grain complexes — is the largest addressable category. Director Bloor asked whether any operational changes were being proposed at this time. CFO Grieve responded that management was not presenting any program or measure for approval at this meeting, that any measure touching customer-facing operations or customer contracts would be brought to the Board with a written memorandum, and that management expected to return with a defined program later in the quarter. Director Fontaine cautioned that contractual service specifications at leased sites should be reviewed before any operational change is considered. THE BOARD TOOK NO ACTION on the energy cost review and DEFERRED the topic to a future meeting pending a detailed management memorandum.

4. Insurance renewal. The Board approved the property and casualty renewal program as presented by the broker, on motion duly made and seconded, 7-0.

5. Other business. None.

6. Adjournment. The meeting adjourned at 11:02 AM.

Respectfully submitted,
S. Marchetti, Secretary

documents.body:
MERIDIAN GRAIN COOPERATIVE, INC. — WORKING DRAFT — NOT FINAL
Watermarked: DRAFT — SUPERSEDED — DO NOT CITE
May 12, 2025
From: O. Brandt, CFO
To: File (litigation working papers)
Re: Preliminary damages walk, Silo Complex 4 event — FIRST PASS, PENDING GRADING AND COVER SETTLEMENT

Status note. This one-page walk was prepared while state grain inspection grading was still underway and before the merchandising desk's cover program had settled. Every figure below is an estimate and every figure below was later replaced. The final destroyed-inventory value is stated in the CFO inventory valuation memorandum of May 20, 2025, and the final cover premium is stated in the merchandising desk cover purchase summary of May 27, 2025. This draft is retained only to show the evolution of the analysis and must not be cited as the cooperative's damages position.

Preliminary walk (as of May 12, superseded):

Component 1 — Destroyed inventory (ESTIMATE). Assumed all eighteen affected lots grade to sample grade; applied a flat indicative discount to the March average board price without basis, protein or salvage adjustment. Working estimate: 6,100,000 dollars. Grading was completed May 8 and salvage auctions settled May 16; this estimate does not reflect either.

Component 2 — Cover purchases (ROUGH ESTIMATE). Desk had executed six of an expected eleven cover trades at drafting. Straight-line extrapolation of the premium on the executed trades, no freight differential: 1,800,000 dollars. The desk cautioned at the time that out-of-position freight would move this number materially.

PRELIMINARY AGGREGATE (SUPERSEDED): 7,900,000 dollars.

Items intentionally excluded pending counsel guidance: disposal and fumigation charges; extra elevation and handling; interest; any claim respecting the 2025-26 storage season. Counsel to advise on recoverability before any of these are added to a demand.

O. Brandt
Chief Financial Officer
